_info.comment: EIP-225 Clique: the authorized signer set is a pure function of the header chain, and this file is that function's vector set. Each vector is a genesis carrying an initial signer list in extraData, a sequence of sealed headers casting votes through the coinbase and nonce fields, and the signer set a correct client derives at the head. Four vectors instead expect a REFUSAL -- an unauthorized signer, and three shapes of the recent-signer rule.
_info.whyThisIsProposalScopedAndNotNetworkScop: Nothing here carries a chain id or a family's upgrade labels. Clique's voting rule is the same on every network that runs it, which is what `proposals/` is for and why this is the first file in it. A Clique network fixture -- one asserting a particular chain's genesis signer set or period -- would be network-scoped and does not belong here.
_info.howAHarnessReadsThis: Build the genesis from `genesisSigners` (sorted ascending, 20 bytes each, at offset 32 of a 32+20n+65 byte extraData) and confirm your genesis hash equals `genesis.hash` before going further -- if it does not, nothing below will agree and the cause is your genesis, not the vectors. Then decode each entry of `headers` from its `rlp` and import them in order. `expectedFailure` is an EMPTY STRING, not null, when a vector expects no refusal -- and `expectedFailureAtIndex` is then ABSENT rather than null. Test the string's length, not its nullity. Where it is empty, compare your derived signer set at the head against `expectedSigners`; where it is set, the import MUST fail at `expectedFailureAtIndex` with that condition. `signerLabel`, `votedLabel` and `authorize` are provenance, not inputs -- a harness that reads them instead of recovering the signer from the seal asserts nothing.
_info.theKeysAreDerivedNotRandom: sk(label) = keccak256("fukuii-tests/eip-225/" + label), reduced as a secp256k1 scalar. This is the whole reason the upstream scenario table could never be a fixture: it calls crypto.GenerateKey() per run, so its addresses -- and therefore every seal, every hash and the sort order of every signer set -- differ on every execution. Fixing the derivation is what turns the table into data.
_info.inTurnIsRECORDEDNotASSERTEDHere: Every header carries the difficulty the in-turn/out-of-turn rule requires, so these chains are valid under a client that checks it. The rule itself is asserted by clique_seal_difficulty.json, which is where the negative cases live. `inTurn` here is the derived fact that made each difficulty what it is.
_info.oracle: ethereum/go-ethereum consensus/clique, RUN not read. Every expectation is this engine's own output: the signer set is snap.signers() at the head, and each refusal is the error InsertChain actually returned. The generator is .local/tools/clique/ in this repository.
_info.crossImplementation: Generated a second time against etclabscore/core-geth's lineage (white-b0x/core-geth @ 26975d6a1) and the two outputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL, comparison calibrated against a deliberately mutated copy that reported a difference. That is agreement WITHIN one lineage and is not independent evidence: core-geth's consensus/clique differs from go-ethereum's only in type plumbing, and verifySeal -- which holds both rules this suite tests -- is byte-identical. What it does establish is that the Ethereum Classic fork changed no Clique semantics, so the file rests on upstream go-ethereum rather than on a fork of it.
_info.whatIsNOTAnIndependentOracleHere: CLOSED, 2026-08-26. Nethermind (C#, root commit sharing no ancestry with go-ethereum or besu) at 0acff53275 derived the signer set for all 20 non-refusal vectors through its own ISnapshotManager.GetOrCreateSnapshot(..).Signers -- computed from the header chain with real ECDSA recovery, not supplied -- and agreed with go-ethereum on every one. It also agreed on all 4 refusal vectors, and on WHICH condition each violates: upstream_20 unauthorized and not recently-signed, upstream_21/_22/_23 recently-signed and not unauthorized. 24 of 24.
_info.wrongBuildMethod: Six single-rule defects were introduced into ethereum/go-ethereum's consensus/clique one at a time, each verified to change the source AND to still compile before its score was accepted -- an inert or non-compiling patch produces a clean NOT-CAUGHT indistinguishable from a real coverage gap. The unmodified build is the control and catches nothing (24/24 pass).

wrongBuildScores.vote_majority_off_by_one: 17/24 -- tally.Votes > len(Signers)/2 relaxed to >=. The file's core rule.
wrongBuildScores.recent_signer_limit_off_by_one: 3/24, and they are exactly upstream_21, _22 and _23, the three recent-signature vectors. len(Signers)/2+1 reduced to /2 in verifySeal.
wrongBuildScores.epoch_does_not_reset_votes: 1/24, and it is exactly upstream_19, the epoch-transition vector. The votes/tally clear at number%Epoch==0 was removed.
wrongBuildScores.dropped_signers_votes_not_discarded: 2/24, and they are exactly upstream_13 and _14, the two deauthorized-voter vectors. The loop that uncasts a dropped signer's votes was disabled.
wrongBuildScores.difficulty_inturn_branch_only: 0/24 -- this file cannot see the difficulty rule at all, which is why clique_seal_difficulty.json exists rather than folding into this one.

_info.theAttributionIsThePoint: A count alone would not establish that these vectors cover distinct failure modes. Three of the four defects are caught by exactly the vectors that target them and by no others, which is the difference between a reasoned claim of coverage and a measured one.
_info.aHARNESSMUSTREADchainConfigFIRST: These headers are London-era and carry 16 RLP fields. A client configured outside that window fails at decode, before any rule is reached. `chainConfig` states exactly what to set; do not infer it from the genesis fields.
_info.whatTheBesuRunDIDEstablishForThisFile: Indirectly but not trivially: besu recomputed six of this suite's header hashes identically and recovered proposers from seals produced by go-ethereum. The encoding these vectors depend on -- extraData layout, seal hash, RLP -- is therefore confirmed across two implementations even though this file's own rule is not yet.
_info.thisWordingWasWRONGAndASecondLanguageFou: This field was documented as null until 2026-08-26. It is an empty string, and the reference harness could not catch the error because it is Go, where the natural check is == "" and the documentation was never the thing it read. A C# harness written from this prose crashed on the first vector. Recorded because it is the clearest available argument for cross-implementation verification: the defect was in the SPECIFICATION of the fixture, invisible to any harness sharing its author's assumptions.
_info.whyNETHERMINDAndNotBesuClosedThis: besu derives validators through BlockValidatorProvider and VoteTallyCache wired at the application layer, so reaching the derivation from a unit test means standing up much of a node; handing it a validator set instead would be circular, because the derivation IS this file's subject. Nethermind exposes the same derivation through a public interface driven by an in-memory BlockTree and MemDb. The seam a client offers, not the language or the lineage, decided which could answer -- and that is worth knowing before choosing an oracle for the next mechanism.
_info.theRequiredCALLORDERThisSurfaced: Nethermind's HasSignedRecently indexes Signers directly and throws when the signer is absent, so authorization must be tested first. That is not a defect: go-ethereum's verifySeal checks membership before walking recents in exactly the same order. Two implementations independently requiring the same order is itself a small conformance finding, and a harness that calls them the other way round crashes rather than answering.
_info.theNethermindREFIsOursButTheCODEWasUPSTR: Correction, 2026-08-27. Nethermind 0acff53275, named in this project's Clique work, exists only on the main branch of the maintainer's fork (white-b0x/nethermind) and is a docs commit; a pristine NethermindEth/nethermind clone cannot resolve it. The EVIDENCE is unaffected, measured: Nethermind.Consensus.Clique hashes to 86a6524bc493 and Nethermind.Clique.Test to 44cad515b7c9, both IDENTICAL at the cited ref and at the merge-base with the upstream branch, c9924bb3a0 -- itself an upstream commit. Calibrated in the same run: src/Nethermind/Chains/classic.json, which the overlay does change, reports DIFFERS. **Cite c9924bb3a0 to reproduce this from upstream clones.**
_info.whyThisCorrectionExistsAtAll: On this machine reference-material/* is upstream third-party work and work/repos/* is the maintainer's own. A cross-implementation citation has to name a ref an outside reader can resolve, and a fork's main branch is not one. The test is mechanical: `git branch -a --contains <sha>` -- if the answer is only `main`, the commit is ours; if it includes `upstream`, it is a mirror of the third party.

chainConfig.comment: What a client must configure for its header decoder and validator to accept these chains. Recorded because it is NOT derivable from the vectors, and a wrong guess fails at RLP decode -- which reads as a broken fixture rather than a misconfigured harness.
chainConfig.whyTheFieldCountMatters: 16 fields is the London-era header: 15 pre-London, 16 with baseFeePerGas, 17 once Shanghai adds withdrawalsRoot, 20 at Cancun. A client configured outside that window cannot decode these headers at all, and the failure looks nothing like a consensus disagreement.
chainConfig.notActivated: No time-based fork. Shanghai, Cancun, Prague and everything later are unset -- which is what keeps the header at 16 fields.
chainConfig.terminalTotalDifficulty: 0x7fffffffffffffff -- effectively unreachable, so these chains never merge and stay under the Clique engine throughout.
chainConfig.chainIdIsNOTAnInputAndThatWasMEASURED: The whole vector set was regenerated with chainId 61 and the output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to chainId 1. That is the evidence for filing this under proposals/ rather than under a network: no chain id reaches the rule, and the value above is a generator artifact a harness may set to anything.
chainConfig.genesisAllocIsEMPTY: stateRoot 0x56e81f171bcc55a6ff8345e692c0f86e5b48e01b996cadc001622fb5e363b421 is the empty trie root. There are no accounts, no transactions and no ommers in any vector.

vectors.name: upstream_00
vectors.comment: Single signer, no votes cast

vectors.name: upstream_01
vectors.comment: Single signer, voting to add two others (only accept first, second needs 2 votes)

vectors.name: upstream_02
vectors.comment: Two signers, voting to add three others (only accept first two, third needs 3 votes already)

vectors.name: upstream_03
vectors.comment: Single signer, dropping itself (weird, but one less cornercase by explicitly allowing this)

vectors.name: upstream_04
vectors.comment: Two signers, actually needing mutual consent to drop either of them (not fulfilled)

vectors.name: upstream_05
vectors.comment: Two signers, actually needing mutual consent to drop either of them (fulfilled)

vectors.name: upstream_06
vectors.comment: Three signers, two of them deciding to drop the third

vectors.name: upstream_07
vectors.comment: Four signers, consensus of two not being enough to drop anyone

vectors.name: upstream_08
vectors.comment: Four signers, consensus of three already being enough to drop someone

vectors.name: upstream_09
vectors.comment: Authorizations are counted once per signer per target

vectors.name: upstream_10
vectors.comment: Authorizing multiple accounts concurrently is permitted

vectors.name: upstream_11
vectors.comment: Deauthorizations are counted once per signer per target

vectors.name: upstream_12
vectors.comment: Deauthorizing multiple accounts concurrently is permitted

vectors.name: upstream_13
vectors.comment: Votes from deauthorized signers are discarded immediately (deauth votes)

vectors.name: upstream_14
vectors.comment: Votes from deauthorized signers are discarded immediately (auth votes)

vectors.name: upstream_15
vectors.comment: Cascading changes are not allowed, only the account being voted on may change

vectors.name: upstream_16
vectors.comment: Changes reaching consensus out of bounds (via a deauth) execute on touch

vectors.name: upstream_17
vectors.comment: Changes reaching consensus out of bounds (via a deauth) may go out of consensus on first touch

vectors.name: upstream_18
vectors.comment: Ensure that pending votes don't survive authorization status changes. This corner case can only appear if a signer is quickly added, removed and then re-added (or the inverse), while one of the original voters dropped. If a past vote is left cached in the system somewhere, this will interfere with the final signer outcome.

vectors.name: upstream_19
vectors.comment: Epoch transitions reset all votes to allow chain checkpointing

vectors.name: upstream_20
vectors.comment: An unauthorized signer should not be able to sign blocks

vectors.name: upstream_21
vectors.comment: An authorized signer that signed recently should not be able to sign again

vectors.name: upstream_22
vectors.comment: Recent signatures should not reset on checkpoint blocks imported in a batch

vectors.name: upstream_23
vectors.comment: Recent signatures should not reset on checkpoint blocks imported in a new batch (go-ethereum issue 17593). Whilst this seems overly specific and weird, it was a Rinkeby consensus split.
